description: Aura restructure — finish the package re-organization (Step 1 tail + Step 2+) and ship the picobot-discipline modular layout. Master-direct workflow: every story is a SINGLE atomic commit on master, no branches, no PR. Suite must stay green at every commit (go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./...).

userStories.title: Step 1.5a — health → internal/api/health_* with Health* prefix on exports
userStories.description: Move internal/health/{sanitize,server}.go (+tests) into internal/api/ as health_sanitize.go, health_server.go (+tests). Rename package decl to api. To avoid name collisions inside api/, prefix exports: Server→HealthServer, ServerConfig→HealthServerConfig, ComponentHealth→HealthComponent, SanitizeHandler→HealthSanitizeHandler, NewServer→NewHealthServer, NewSanitizeHandler→NewHealthSanitizeHandler, StatusProvider→HealthStatusProvider, TelegramInfo→HealthTelegramInfo. Critical: rename pattern must be applied in DEPENDENCY ORDER (longest names first) to avoid double-prefix bug (e.g. SanitizeHandler→HealthSanitizeHandler must NOT then match the substring inside NewHealthSanitizeHandler).

userStories.title: Step 1.5c — auth as internal/api/auth/ sub-package (break tools→api cycle)
userStories.description: Master plan wanted flat auth→api merge, but that creates a cycle: internal/tools/auth.go uses auth.TokenWriter; with auth folded into api, tools imports api, api/router.go imports swarm, swarm imports agent, agent imports tools → cycle. Solution: move auth files to internal/api/auth/ as a SUB-PACKAGE (still `package auth`). This way tools keeps importing `internal/api/auth` (now under api/) without importing api itself. internal/auth/ becomes internal/api/auth/. Move 5 files (middleware.go, middleware_test.go, pending_test.go, store.go, store_test.go) preserving names + package auth declaration. Update all callers' import paths: `"github.com/aura/aura/internal/auth"` → `"github.com/aura/aura/internal/api/auth"`.

userStories.notes: Honors master plan intent (auth moves under api) without breaking layering. tools/auth.go imports internal/api/auth which is a leaf sub-package; api/router.go can still import auth via the new path. No imports api from tools, no cycle.
